problem: Large language models face significant limitations in music-related applications due to a lack of music-specific knowledge in their training data, making text-only Music Question Answering (MQA) challenging (p.1). Additionally, current text-only QA benchmarks inadequately cover artist-centric information needs such as complete discographies and collaboration networks (p.2).
methodology: The authors propose MusT-RAG, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that adapts general-purpose LLMs for the music domain by retrieving relevant passages from a music-specific vector database during inference (p.1). They also introduce a RAG-style fine-tuning approach utilizing context, question, and answer triples to train the model on how to incorporate external contextual information during generation (p.3).
dataset: The study utilizes MusWikiDB, a comprehensive music-specific vector database containing 31K pages and 629.2K passages collected from Wikipedia across seven categories (p.3). They also introduce ArtistMus, a benchmark of 1,000 multiple-choice questions focusing on artist-related QA, and use the TrustMus benchmark for out-of-domain evaluation (p.4, 5).
results: On the ArtistMus benchmark, RAG fine-tuning achieved an 82.4% factual score and a 92.0% contextual score, outperforming GPT-4o by 15.0% in factual performance while maintaining comparable contextual performance (p.5, 6). On the out-of-domain TrustMus benchmark, the RAG fine-tuned model achieved an overall score of 41.5%, providing a 5.7% performance improvement over the zero-shot baseline (p.5, 6). Furthermore, MusWikiDB achieved a 10x faster retrieval speed and 5.9% higher performance compared to the general Wikipedia corpus (p.6).
key_findings: MusT-RAG effectively addresses the music domain adaptation problem by leveraging RAG to retrieve relevant context without requiring full model retraining (p.1). RAG-style fine-tuning outperforms conventional fine-tuning by improving both factual accuracy and contextual understanding (p.6). Additionally, MusWikiDB proved substantially more effective and computationally efficient than general Wikipedia corpora for music QA (p.1).
title: MUST-RAG: MUSical Text Question Answering with Retrieval Augmented Generation
